edits.old: MongoDB recommends reusing one MongoClient per process. Combined with Cloud Run's independently scaled instances, this means each instance has its own process-local client pool and the service's potential connection count grows with active instances and the connected topology. This is a capacity inference; it does not mean every pool reaches its ceiling. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)
edits.new: MongoDB recommends creating one MongoClient per process and reusing it for all operations in that process. Each MongoClient has a connection pool for each server in the topology, plus up to two monitoring connections per server. Cloud Run scales each revision to the number of instances needed for incoming requests. If each instance runs its own application process (an inference, not stated by either source), then each instance has its own client and pools, and the service's potential connection count grows with the number of active instances and the connected topology. This is a capacity inference; it does not mean every pool reaches its ceiling. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools/ ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/about-concurrency

edits.rationale: MongoDB's docs support one client per process and a pool per server in the topology, with monitoring sockets on top. Cloud Run's docs support automatic scaling to as many instances as needed. No source states explicitly that each instance holds its own process-local pool, so that link is an inference the original claim already labels. The statement that this does not mean every pool reaches its ceiling is a qualification, not a checkable fact.

edits.old: Cloud Run concurrency limits simultaneous requests per instance, not MongoDB sockets. For a fixed request volume, lower concurrency can require more instances, while higher concurrency can let fewer instances serve traffic when the application handles parallel work; because client pools are process-local, concurrency changes the number of pools indirectly. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)
edits.new: Cloud Run's maximum concurrent requests setting limits the number of requests processed simultaneously by a given instance. It is not a limit on MongoDB sockets. For the same request volume, lower concurrency forces Cloud Run to use more instances, while higher concurrency can lead to fewer active instances if the application handles parallel work. Because MongoDB client pools are per client (per process) and each pool opens sockets per server, concurrency affects the number of pools only indirectly, by changing the number of instances. This last step is an inference. Sources: https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/about-concurrency ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools/
